parts.t: Otter District is the rural southeast corner of the Township of Langley, south of Fraser Highway and running down to the U.S. border, between Campbell Valley and Aldergrove. Its old centre is the farm crossroads at 248 Street and Fraser Highway, where the farmers’ institute that became the Otter Co-op opened a store in 1946. Most of the land is farmland, so wells, septic and ALR rules shape what a property can be used for.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 9, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate since 2015. Facts come from the Township of Langley, the Langley Heritage Society, Metro Vancouver, the Province and the other sources noted on this page. Boundaries and rules change, so confirm anything important with the Township and the Agricultural Land Commission.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Planning and the ALR in Otter District

parts.t: Farm rules come first here. Check them before you plan a shop, a second house or a business.
Otter falls under the Township’s Rural Plan (Bylaw No. 3250), adopted July 12, 1993.
The Agro-Service Centre at 248 Street and Fraser Highway is limited to uses that work on septic, and to industry directly tied to farming.
About 75% of the Township’s land is in the ALR, and ALR status is set parcel by parcel.
Bertrand Creek flows south toward the Nooksack. Streamside setbacks start at the top of bank, for example 30 m for a Class A watercourse.
The 2009 Water Management Plan named the Aldergrove aquifer among the more heavily used aquifers with falling water levels.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Otter District

parts.t: Check the parcel on the ALC map and get the zoning from the Township before you plan any new building.
Ask for well depth, a flow test and a water quality test. The Township’s Private Well Network offers discounted testing.
Locate the tank and field, and get the age and service records.
Confirm permits for barns, arenas, shops and any second home.
Farm traffic, livestock and farm-related businesses near 248 Street are normal here. Visit at different times of day.
Look for covenants, rights of way and shared lanes.
